#4303. EU pushes back Tesla ‘Full Self-Driving’ vote meeting again, now set for December 15

The EU committee that could approve Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving,” now sold in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving, across the whole bloc won’t meet on December 1 as planned. The meeting is now December 15.

A European Commission spokesperson confirmed the new date to Reuters. The Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) has already discussed Tesla’s file at two meetings without putting it to a vote.

Two weeks isn’t much on its own. But it’s the latest in a long line of European dates that didn’t hold.

In late 2025, Tesla told owners the Dutch regulator RDW had “committed” to approving FSD in February 2026. The RDW publicly corrected it. The Dutch approval came on April 10. Tesla then pointed owners to an EU-wide vote on October 6, and the TCMV agenda for that meeting had no vote on it.

Even the new date took a minute to settle. Belgium’s Flanders transport ministry first said the meeting had moved to December 7 before the Commission clarified it’s December 15. Nobody has given a reason for the change.

And a meeting isn’t a vote. The committee can discuss the file again and push the decision into 2027. Elon Musk said on Tesla’s Q3 call in October that he’d be surprised if EU-wide approval took longer than the first quarter of 2027.

EU-wide approval needs at least 15 of the 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU’s population.

Twelve countries have recognized the Dutch approval so far: the Netherlands, Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and, last week, Italy, where Tesla has started the rollout. Using Eurostat population figures, we count those 12 at roughly 29% of the EU’s population.

Germany is the obvious next yes. Berlin got Tesla to drop the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe and then cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in exchange for its support. That would bring the yes camp to about 47%.

So Tesla still needs France, or both Spain and Poland, to get over 65%. Not a sure thing. Sweden asked the EU in June to reject the system unless Tesla removed the ability to drive above the posted limit at all.

There’s also a catch for owners. According to Reuters, an EU-level rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted. If the vote fails, drivers in Italy, the Netherlands, and the 10 other countries who are paying for the system today could lose it.

A two-week slip in a Brussels committee calendar isn’t too bad, but the delays are adding up. It’s December, the committee has other files, and nothing Reuters reported points to a problem specific to Tesla.

Article and headline should consistently refer to it as Tesla Assisted Driving as that is the name which Tesla has agreed to use in the EU. I think the other big question for EU approval is how easily can the driver avoid paying attention to the road.

We also don’t think most owners realize what’s at stake. If this vote goes the wrong way, the national approvals go with it. Italian owners who just got the system would lose it a few weeks later.

What would help Tesla’s case more than a new name and a lower speed cap is data. The RDW still hasn’t published its test results, and Tesla has never released disengagement data in Europe or anywhere else. Governments on the fence, like Sweden, want to see evidence the system is safe, not a rebrand.

December 15 is the next date to watch. Does Tesla walk into that room with Germany, France, or Spain on board, or does this slide into 2027?

#4302. EVs Outsold Gas And Diesel Cars Combined In The EU In October

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The European Union registered about 24,000 more new cars last month than in October 2025. Fully electric cars alone added more than 106,000 to the tally, while sales of gasoline-only cars fell by nearly 30% and diesel sales dropped by 31%.

According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), the EU registered 279,799 fully electric passenger cars in October, marking a significant year-over-year jump of 61.4%. Gasoline cars accounted for 158,970 registrations, and diesels added another 51,177.

This means that for every three new gas or diesel cars that hit EU roads last month, roughly four new EVs joined them. ACEA counts hybrids separately, including mild hybrids with a gasoline or diesel engine.

One year ago, in October 2025, the big news was that plug-in hybrids had overtaken diesel through the first ten months across the EU, UK and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) markets. Within the EU itself, fully electric cars still accounted for just 16.4% of registrations over that period. Even in October alone, gasoline cars comfortably outsold EVs, even before you added diesels.

Then came December 2025, when EVs outsold gasoline cars across the EU for the first time. By the third quarter of 2026, EVs had passed gas and diesel combined. The margin back then was about 55,000 cars across July, August and September. In October, EVs cleared that margin in a single month.

Significant EV sales growth in Germany and France explains much of the jump. Between them, they saw about 69,500 more electric car registrations than in October 2025, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the EU’s increase.

In Germany, more than 94,000 new EVs hit the road in October, making up 37% of the country’s new-car market that month. France registered nearly 62,000 EVs, enough to outsell conventional hybrids, which accounted for about 55,400 cars.

The same shift looks rather different in Romania. EV registrations rose almost 47% in October even as the overall car market shrank. That was enough for electric cars to beat gasoline cars by just seven registrations, 1,495 to 1,488. Add diesels back in and combustion still wins. Meanwhile, Romanians registered more than 6,600 conventional hybrids, comfortably ahead of either.

This reflects a broader trend across the EU, where hybrids remain the most popular choice. Full and mild hybrids accounted for 36% of registrations through October, against 23.4% for fully electric cars. Gas and diesel also retain a combined lead so far this year. What’s changed is how small that lead has become. At this point last year, gas and diesel together outsold EVs by more than two to one.

Ten months into 2026, the tally stands at 2.62 million to 2.21 million, and the most recent month went decisively to the cars with a plug and no engine.

The number of electric models on offer in Europe grew by about half in a year, and many of the new additions were small and affordable models. Buyers shopping for a small hatchback now have the Renault 5, Cupra Raval and Volkswagen ID. Polo to choose from.

Actually getting one is another matter. VW has reportedly taken more than 50,000 ID. Polo orders, with German buyers facing wait times of up to 21 months for the cheapest version.

#4301. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4299. Driven: 2028 Porsche 718 Boxster EV Prototype Wags Its Tail Like a Mid-Engine Sports Car

The Boxster’s rear-biased weight distribution, which is unusual for an EV, makes it handle like a sports car should.

There’s still a lot that Porsche won’t divulge about its forthcoming 2028 718 Boxster EV, including horsepower, battery capacity, range, pricing, or even its final, un-camouflaged looks. But after some seat time around the handling course at the Porsche Experience Center Los Angeles, we now know what it feels like at—and a little bit beyond—its cornering limits.

Whether you’re welcoming the Boxster’s EV transition or bemoaning the loss of its internal-combustion engines, particularly the iconic flat-six, we think anyone who drives the next-generation 983 Boxster will agree it’s fantastic. The steering, inherited from the 992.2 911 Carrera GTS, is eager and sharp, and rear-axle steering will also be available. You can feel the Boxster’s rear-biased weight distribution in the way its rear end steps out when lifting off the throttle.

In other words, this new EV feels like a mid-engine Boxster, because that’s where the weight is concentrated. Other than some hypercars, such as the Rimac Nevera, the forthcoming electric Boxster rides atop one of the first EV platforms built around a two-seat sports car. The 800-volt battery pack lives entirely behind the passenger cabin, in the place the engine used to reside, which leads to a 40/60 front/rear weight distribution, similar to the gas-powered Boxster’s 45/55 split. And since there’s no battery under the floor, you sit as low as you would in any other sports car.

See all results for new 2028 Porsche 718 EV for sale near 90044

We drove what will become the top Boxster model when it goes on sale after its formal debut in early 2027, but Porsche wouldn’t confirm what it will be called. S? GTS? These models wear Pirelli P Zero R Elect tires—and for the first time—mount on staggered-diameter wheels just like the latest 911. The tires measure 255/35ZR-20 up front and 305/30ZR-21 in back, which is more meat than even the last 718 Spyder RS. The company isn’t saying how much power this Boxster’s single rear motor will make—all electric Boxsters will be rear-drive only—but they do claim the sprint to 60 mph will require less than 3.0 seconds. After experiencing being pinned to the seat by a few launch-control starts, the new Boxster feels every bit that quick.

Porsche says this will be the quickest, most powerful Boxster with the highest cornering and braking performance, with a center of gravity that’s—no surprise—much lower than before. We can attest to feeling tons of grip, but can we feel the EV’s added weight? As the Boxster slithered through transitions and dove into apexes, we can’t say it felt heavy, although the squealing from its wide tires sounded at times more tortured than those we recall from the just-over-3000-pound gas-powered Boxster. Porsche says the Boxster EV’s curb weight will fall somewhere within that of the 911 lineup, which ranges from the 3350-pound Carrera to the 4000-pound Turbo S Cabriolet. Here’s hoping it’s toward the lower end of that range, which would be very light for an EV.

See all results for new 2028 Porsche 718 EV for sale near 90044

While this new electric version looks like a Boxster and the low seating position feels like a Boxster, with a forward view of a quickly disappearing hood, Porsche wanted to add some more nostalgic tie-ins by way of fabricated engine noises and simulated shifts. The Taycan got a similar E-Shift feature earlier this year, but while the Taycan’s engine noises weren’t modeled after a specific engine, the Boxster’s very much pays homage to its past. The Boxster’s E-Shift, which is controlled by a knob on the steering wheel and can shift automatically or be controlled by steering wheel paddles, mimics the 981 Boxster GTS’s 3.4-liter flat-six, which Porsche engineers say is the high-water mark for flat-six wails. They told us emissions compromises to the most recent flat-sixes made them choose that one from circa 2015. That said, there’s a bit of revisionist history going on with the electric Boxster’s 8000-rpm “redline” versus the actual 7600-rpm redline in its 981 muse. Either way, the noise emanating from the two speakers—one inside the cabin, one outside—absolutely sounds like a flat-six.

Although the synthesized sound is a solid re-creation, we do think it would be easy to identify the real from the facsimile in a blindfolded test. There’s a lot of nuance going on in the sounds of a flat-six belting to redline—intake and exhaust noise, valve and other mechanical clatter—and it’s hard to generate all of that from a couple speakers. That said, after doing a few hot laps with the system on, we believe it adds to the experience, and it felt weird to switch over to silent and shift-free lapping. We think we’d use this more in a sports car like the Boxster than in the four-door Taycan sedan.

What else did we learn? As before, the 983 Boxster has both front and rear trunks, and its NACS charge port, which is hidden behind a powered door in the middle of the rear bumper, is the first from Porsche to accommodate both AC and DC charging. Today’s Cayenne and Taycan electrics have separate ports for AC and DC with the NACS only handling DC charging.

Officially, there won’t be any gas-powered Boxster variants, but who knows what the lifecycle might hold, especially if early sales disappoint. After all, remember when the previous generation went four-cylinder only, but then the flat-six made a reappearance a few years later? While we’re as sad as anyone to see the flat-six and manual transmission leave the Boxster lineup, we think that anyone who drives the new one will agree it’s a great-handling sports car.

#4298. I've Driven Dozens Of Chinese Cars. Americans Are Missing Out On These 4 Features

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Chinese cars are famous (or infamous, if you’re not so keen on the integration of tech into cars) for serving up a stunning amount of features and technology. As the country’s car companies race to one-up one another in a fiercely competitive market, they’ve rolled out cars that can float, deploy built-in drones, and hop in place.

It’s no wonder that many Americans are eagerly waiting for the day when they can take one of these cars home themselves. After driving dozens of Chinese EV and plug-in hybrid models, I’ve identified a few common features that I think U.S. drivers are missing out on.

Electronic automatic doors aren’t a China-specific innovation. Doors that open and close at the touch of a button are options (or standard features) on big, pricey cars like the BMW iX5, Rolls-Royce Spectre, Cadillac Escalade IQ, or the Tesla Model X.

However, while the feature tends to be primarily for cars that are deep in luxury territory in the U.S., it’s ubiquitous in China, specifically among premium EV models. All of Zeekr’s cars, for example, have the feature either standard or as an option, including the Zeekr X, a small crossover that starts at the equivalent of under $30,000.

Automatic doors aren’t necessarily everyone’s cup of tea, but I would argue that they make a car feel more expensive and luxurious. It didn’t take me long to get used to the process of touching a button to open the door, sitting down, and then pressing the brake to close it. Sitting in the Zeekr X, it felt like I was in my own affordable version of a Rolls-Royce—at least in one respect.

China’s car market is also full of less practical features that are simply meant to be charming and cute. For example, lots of models come with fun cartoon characters and mascots baked in.

Consider Nio’s Nomi. This AI-powered mascot takes the form of an orb on the dash with eyes that blink and look around. It not only acts as an in-car Amazon Alexa-style assistant that can answer questions or tell jokes, but it reacts to things you do, like playing music. Its design has captured the creativity of Nio drivers all around China; there’s a whole culture and third-party ecosystem around making cute outfits and accessories for Nomi.

Nio’s physical representation in the interior may be unique in China’s car market, but the concept of an in-car mascot is not. Xiaomi, Geely, Chery, and many others have cute little robot guys or cartoon animals meant to assist the driver while also giving the car some extra personality. Here in the States, we have Rivian’s Gear Guard, but that’s about it.

It has been a long while since I’ve been behind the wheel of a Nio, but I still think fondly of the cowboy hat-wearing Nomi that accompanied me on the drive in the Nio ES6.

Low-stakes car personalization is a huge thing in China, and it’s a delight to see in the wild. Take a gander at traffic in any given Chinese city, and it’s not too hard to find a car with customized taillights or headlights that show emojis or text.

An IM Motors crossover can display customizable messages on its back window that can be changed to, for example, say “thank you” when another car lets you merge ahead of them. Aito’s heart-shaped brake lights make me smile. The Lynk & Co 900’s high-resolution LED screen lets you put your own handwriting on the front of the car.

To some, all of this may seem silly and unnecessary, but I think it lends some personality and flair to an otherwise uninteresting part of the car.

Climate-controlled compartments aren’t super unique. In the U.S., cars have been offered with refrigerators before, but not on the same level as what I’ve seen in China. For example, the SkyNomad N90 SUV’s center-console-mounted combo fridge and warmer can go all the way down to 21 degrees Fahrenheit—to act as a freezer—or all the way up to 122 degrees, which can keep food pretty dang warm.

The fridge-warmer combo in the Nio ET9 gets nearly as cold, but can warm to a toasty 131 degrees. The high-end Denza Z9 GT has two such compartments, one in the front center console, and one in the rear between the two rear seats.

It’s well documented that Chinese cars are beating the world on EV cost and technology. I’d argue they’re also winning on whimsy. After driving lots of Chinese cars, it’s clear that these brands are willing to try out new ideas that might seem juvenile or not important—but result in a car with way more personality than your average EV from a Western manufacturer.

In China, you can have your cake and eat it too: a car that charges to nearly full in less than ten minutes, with a cute mascot that makes you laugh and a compartment that warms up your lunch. I think that’s pretty cool.

#4297. The Suzuki Ignis is back, and this time it will be a low-cost EV sold globally [Images]

Suzuki offered a first look at the all-new Ignis, its first compact EV designed specifically for global markets.

The first-generation Ignis went on sale back in 2000 as a three- and five-door hatchback, and in 2016, Suzuki reintroduced it as a compact crossover.

After discontinuing the gas-powered version just last year, Suzuki is now bringing the Ignis back. This time, as a fully electric compact EV.

Suzuki revealed the all-new Ignis EV on Wednesday, deeming it the brand’s “first compact EV for global markets.”

The electric city car is based on the original Ignis and clearly draws inspiration from the e Sky, Suzuki’s first kei EV that debuted last month in Japan.

Unlike the e Sky, the new Ignis EV is designed for global markets, including Europe. Suzuki said the Ignis was developed under the concept of “Easy to Switch,” which, as you can guess, means it’s designed to make it easy for drivers to switch from a gas-powered car to electric.

To ensure it can handle urban areas and winding roads in Europe and other regions, Suzuki put the electric city car through “extensive testing” on public roads.

Suzuki fine-tuned the chassis and power delivery specifically for the different road conditions and needs of drivers in major global markets.

The global Ignis EV is also slightly larger than the e Sky, measuring 3,570 mm long, 1,565 mm wide, and 1,635 mm tall, with a 2,460 mm wheelbase.

It’s built on the same dedicated “HEARTECT-e” EV platform as the e Sky, with a single electric motor that delivers 90 hp (67 kW) and 98 lb-ft (133 Nm) of torque.

The Ignis also uses the same 26 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery as the e SKY. However, Suzuki hasn’t revealed driving range figures yet. Suzuki didn’t specify, but the LFP battery pack used in the e SKY is supplied by BYD’s battery unit to keep costs down.

According to Suzuki, the e SKY for Japan offers a WLTC driving range of up to 310 km (192 miles) and a “class-leading” AC energy consumption rating of 97 Wh/km.

Inside, the new Suzuki Ignis EV adopts a similar setup to the e Sky with a space-maximizing four-seat layout and a wide infotainment display.

Great to have a small car option like this. Let us hope it reaches open global markets at a price similar to the e SKY. That is about the price of the BYD Seagull in Australia today (US13-14k). Unfortunately the Seagull is growing in size so it would be good to have the option of this small Suzuki.

It seems likely it will be much more expensive in Europe as all EVs are.

Suzuki will launch the Ignis in Europe and other markets starting in summer 2027. Prices have yet to be announced, but the Ignis will enter an increasingly competitive segment of entry-level compact EVs, including the Renault Twingo, BYD Dolphin Surf, and Honda Super-N.

In Japan, Suzuki’s e SKY undercuts much of the competition with prices starting at just ¥2,120,000 ($13,500).

For context, the Renault Twingo E-Tech starts at under €19,490 ($21,500) in Europe and £14,745 in the UK. BYD’s Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,990 ($25,500) and £18,675 ($24,500) in the UK, while the Honda Super-N starts at £18,995 ($25,000) in the UK.

Which compact EV would you drive? Let us know in the comments. Unfortunately, none of them will be coming to the US.

#4296. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4295. New York Bans Post-Purchase Subscriptions on Vehicles

Monthly payments for heated seats? Not in the state of New York.

Are you paying a subscription fee for hardware already installed on your car? Not for much longer, you’re not. At least, not if you live in New York. Governor Kathy Hochul just signed a bill prohibiting automakers, dealers, and other third parties from charging subscription fees for vehicle features that use pre-installed components or hardware. Those heated seats you’re paying for? Get ready to cancel that subscription. That remote start you buy each winter? Treat yourself to an expensive latte from that cafe you like instead.

See all results for used cars for sale near 19085

The new law (S.9348A/A.10411A) doesn’t stop automakers from charging subscriptions entirely, but it does stop them from being able to charge recurring payments for hardware that doesn’t cause them any recurring costs.

Hochul’s office specifically pointed to heated seats, enhanced navigation, hands-free driving, and entertainment options. Heated seats are pretty cut and dry, but hands-free driving poses an interesting question. Systems such as Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD), GM’s Super Cruise, and Ford’s Blue Cruise all require customers to pay for a subscription to operate. All three systems work with the hardware installed on their respective vehicles, but the automakers could—and likely will—argue that they have recurring costs to keep the systems updated and safe.

Car and Driver reached out to Governor Hochul’s office for clarification on how the law will affect hands-free driving systems. We will update this story if we hear back. Meanwhile, the new law will go into effect on February 27, 2027, giving automakers and third-party companies time to enter into compliance.

#4294. $30,000 Ford Fathom: Inside The Structural LFP Battery That Makes It All Possible

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In a small corner between two conference rooms at the 2-million-square feet BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, Ford brought the upcoming Fathom electric truck’s battery pack for journalists to look at.

The Fathom will get something that’s rare in the U.S. but common on high-tech EVs in China: low-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) cells in a prismatic form factor. That combination is a key enabler of the Fathom's $29,495 starting price, and Ford said it does more than just cut costs.

Charles Poon, the vice president of vehicle hardware engineering at Ford, said the prismatic LFP cells will allow the Fathom to be low-cost and fun-to-drive.

“Those two are what enable us to deliver an affordable structure for the vehicle,” Poon said during a media roundtable at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan last week. It allowed Ford to “take out a lot of components from the vehicle and still be able to be a very fun driving very stiff vehicle,” he said.

Most EVs in the U.S. use cylindrical nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) cells. It's a well-established chemistry and form factor, known for the high energy density that gives EVs long driving range.

Chinese LFP technology, however, has narrowed the gap to NMC in energy density and performance in recent years, while keeping a cost advantage because it forgoes expensive raw materials like nickel and cobalt. That combination is why Chinese EVs offer impressive range and fast charging at affordable prices.

The cells made at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan use technology licensed from CATL, the world's largest battery maker. Ford said the cell design is unique to the company and not something available in CATL's global portfolio. LFP batteries are 20-30% cheaper than NMC ones, Ford said, which made them a good fit for a low-cost EV like the Fathom.

The Fathom's cells are also structural and use a cell-to-pack design, meaning they are installed directly in the pack without modules. Ford said this allowed 20% better packaging efficiency compared to its first-generation EVs like the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning, since larger cells mean fewer of them are needed, which simplifies assembly.

The cells are load bearing, too. Ford said the battery structure handles 60% of the vehicle's load, and 40% of that passes through the cells. Ford engineers said this allowed an even lower center of gravity, which improves the Fathom's overall stiffness and supposedly makes it fun to drive.

Cell-to-pack designs raise a concern about repairability. They aren't as easy to service as module-based packs and can require replacing the whole battery, which can be expensive once a vehicle is out of warranty.

I asked Ford engineers how they plan to address potential cell failures. They pointed to extensive testing, including more than 1,400 process and quality controls in the production system, validation testing in temperatures from -40 degrees Celsius to 60C, nail penetration and collision tests, and environmental testing on equipment like hydraulic shakers that simulate vehicle behavior on the road.

One part of the battery will be repairable: the electronics. On most EVs, the electronics sit in a penthouse on top of the pack. On the Fathom, they are mounted behind the battery, which keeps the pack fully flat and opens up more interior room. They can be accessed, repaired or replaced without lowering the pack.

All said, most buyers likely won't know or care what LFP or prismatic means. They'll care about range, charging speed, and whether the battery lasts. That is where Ford's approach will be tested when the Fathom goes on sale towards the end of next year.

Update 11/25/2026: A Hyundai spokesperson told Electrek that “it’s likely that the IONIQ 3 that was apparently spotted in the US recently was the same unit that was brought in for World Car of the Year’s annual test days” held in Pasadena, California.

A post shared by KindelAuto (@kindelauto)

The update from Hyundai comes after the IONIQ 3 was recently captured driving on public US roads, raising speculation, or perhaps hope, that it will come to the States after all.

The model spotted in the images from KindelAuto is the IONIQ 3 N Line, a sportier, higher-priced trim.

While it’s among the first sightings in the US, we have seen several Hyundai Motor Group electric vehicles testing in the US that are still not available and likely won’t ever be, such as Kia’s EV5 SUV and PV5 van.

The IONIQ 3 is built at Hyundai Motor’s Izmit, Turkey, plant and is specifically designed for European drivers.

In Europe and the UK, Hyundai offers the IONIQ 3 with two battery packs: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 ($25,000) OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range. That’s including the UK’s £3,750 Electric Car Grant.

The IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.

Measuring 4,155 mm (163.5″) long, 1,800 mm (70.9″) wide, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) high, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), Hyundai’s electric hatch is even smaller than the Kia EV3 and Volkswagen ID.3.

The IONIQ 3 is also Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system.

Hyundai’s new system is more like using a smartphone. It’s based on the Android Automotive OS with apps and customizable screens, similar to Tesla models. It’s available in the IONIQ 3 with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Unlike the larger IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. However, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes around 30 minutes.

In Germany and other European markets, Hyundai’s compact IONIQ 3 starts at about €28,950 ($33,000).

While Hyundai currently has no plans to bring the IONIQ 3 to the US, it does sell the IONIQ 5, built at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside Savannah, GA, alongside the three-row IONIQ 9.

Starting at about $35,000, Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 has remained among the top-selling electric vehicles in the US outside of the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

In fact, Hyundai was just named the “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” by US News & World Report for the first time for 2027.

Too bad Tesla refuses to build something like this. Ford could also make a similar car and bring back the Focus nameplate. I don't understand their management decisions.

Hyundai’s sister company, Kia, also launched the 2027 EV3, which is now on sale starting at just $29,890 in the US.

Want to take a closer look at one? We’ve made it easy for you. You can use the links below to find available Hyundai IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, and Kia EV3 models near you.

#4292. Dragon boy Durin is the star of the show in Genshin Impact's wintry Luna 3 update, launching in early December

Genshin Impact is getting two new characters and a whole host of new content in Version Luna 3, which arrives in under two weeks.

The latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain new powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

#4291. Every Brand Selling Hybrid Vehicles in the U.S. for 2027

Hybrid car sales are at a high, and that means plenty of choices in segments including SUVs, sedans, vans, and sports cars.

For all the talk about electric vehicles over the past several years, the bigger story is the current hybrid wave. From 2024 until the end of September 2026, gas-electric hybrids soared from just over eight percent of new light-duty vehicle sales to 16 percent, or double the share of EVs, according to the Energy Information Administration. After consecutive years of parallel growth that saw battery-electric and gas-electric vehicles rise together starting in 2020, hybrid sales have never been higher while EVs, despite a spurt in 2025 and 2026, are not recovering.

This means that there’s now more choice than ever among hybrid vehicles: nearly every major automaker offers at least one hybrid model, and many of them offer a wide range of hybrids in various body styles from SUVs to sports cars and everything in between. Here’s a guide to all hybrids on sale, across all segments (excluding 48-volt hybrids that are not designed to power a vehicle solely with electric motors).

Every Brand Selling Sports Cars | Every Brand Selling EVs | Best-Looking Cars

Bentley makes the world’s only four-seat plug-in hybrid convertible, the Continental GTC. The ravishing powertrain, standard with 671 horsepower or 771 horsepower in the Speed and Mulliner, isn’t exclusive to the the Continental range, either. The twin-turbo V-8 and its 22-kWh battery pack are shared with the Flying Spur sedan, both of which claim 30 miles of electric range (we did 49 in the Continental). A turbo V-6 and an 18-kWh battery are found in the Bentayga Hybrid SUV.

BMW offers a sextet of plug-in hybrids that throw heavy punches under hard acceleration. The 550e, 750e, and X5 xDrive50e share a 483-hp setup with a turbo inline-six good for between 34 and 44 miles of electric range, while the M5, M5 Touring and XM electrify a twin-turbo V-8 for a total of 717 or 738 horsepower. We expect to see more hybrid setups on the high-performance end of the lineup in the future, although the next-gen M3 is also offering a fully electric variant, signifying a possible shift in BMW’s strategy.

Chevrolet’s sole hybrids are found within the Corvette lineup. The first is the Grand Sport X, which supplements the base Stingray’s 6.7-liter V-8 with a front electric motor for a total of 721 horsepower. The other is the ZR1X, which costs a quarter-million dollars and pumps 1250 horsepower from a turbo 5.5-liter V-8 and a front electric motor. It gets 12 mpg in the city and goes 225 mph. It’s beyond magnificent. Still, Chevy is planning more mainstream hybrids, as the three-row Traverse SUV is poised to get a hybrid variant in the future.

All mid-engine Ferraris come as hybrids—and 869 horsepower is the bare minimum. That’s the output from the twin-turbo flat-plane V-6 and axial-flux motor in the new 296 Speciale. The wedgy 849 Testarossa stuffs a twin-turbo V-8 and triple motors for 1036 horsepower. For $3.7 million, the almighty F80 goes backward in cylinder count (but with a more powerful twin-turbo V-6 and three motors) and forward with F1 tech for 1184 horsepower. Buy a front-engine Ferrari and you’ll have to settle for nonhybrid V-12s and V-8s.

Ford sold some of the industry’s first PHEVs in the 2010s—remember the Fusion Energi?—but no longer offers any hybrid sedans or SUVs. The Escape Hybrid and PHEV are gone. But one of our favorite hybrids on sale is the Maverick compact pickup, which can hit 40-plus mpg in the city with front- or all-wheel drive. The F-150 PowerBoost, which uses a twin-turbo V-6 with an electric motor, is more capable but not as smooth to drive as the Maverick.

The first Genesis hybrids aren’t launching until the 2028 model year in the U.S., but we decided to include them here anyway. The lineup includes the gorgeous G80 mid-size luxury sedan and the stately GV80 mid-size luxury SUV. Their hybrid powertrains both use turbo 2.5-liter inline-fours and represent the next stage of the Hyundai group’s hybrid expertise. The batteries now use liquid instead of air cooling, a seven-speed automatic replaces the six-speed, and the torque output (391 lb-ft) matches the twin-turbo V-6 in the 3.5T trims.

Honda has been into hybrids almost as long as Toyota has (see the 1999 Honda Insight), and the company’s current hybrid powertrain is a gem. With direct drive (no transmission), the two-motor, 2.0-liter inline-four setup is quick, efficient, and downright fun. It’s available on the CR-V, the Civic sedan and hatchback, and the Accord sedan, and it’s the only choice on the Prelude coupe.

While the Elantra Hybrid takes a hiatus until 2028, Hyundai’s next-best mileage champ is the Sonata Hybrid, which can surpass 50 mpg and offers generous rear leg room. Hyundai’s three compact and mid-size SUVs, including a new-gen Tucson, get hybrid versions and all offer all-wheel drive. Unlike many mainstream hybrids, Hyundai employs a six-speed automatic instead of a CVT or direct drive. The Tucson plug-in hybrid is no longer available.

While Jeep axed the plug-in hybrid 4xe trims of the Wrangler and Grand Cherokee, an extended-range series hybrid is coming to the Grand Wagoneer with a whopping 647 horsepower. The hybrid-only Cherokee compact SUV comes with only 210 horsepower but up to an estimated 39 mpg city rating.

Like Hyundai, Kia’s diversity of gas, hybrid, and electric powertrains has paid off in spades in terms of sales. There are eight hybrids total in the Kia lineup, with plug-in hybrids available on the Sorento and Sportage (no longer on the Niro). Every SUV has a hybrid option, and so does the Carnival minivan.

Surprised to see Lamborghini peddling hybrids? The brand’s lineup is now entirely hybrid, actually, starting with the plug-in hybrid Urus SUV which comes in 789-hp SE and 801-hp Performante versions. Those SUVs can do an estimated 35 miles on electricity. The 907-hp Temerario is also a plug-in hybrid, offering a pitiful four miles of electric range. But the only hybrid that revs to 10,000 rpm. Then there’s the 1001-hp Revuelto and 1050-hp Revuelto SV which pair a giant V-12 with three electric motors. What a time to be alive.

Leave it to Lexus to combine big power with efficiency. This was the brand that in 2008 gave us the LS600hL, a hybrid flagship that could match the refinement from 12-cylinder German sedans. Now that we live in an SUV world, the LX700h is the modern equivalent—at up to $143,000, it’s the rare four-passenger hybrid SUV with four-wheel drive and a fully reclining rear seat. The TX500h is the next step down (the PHEV is gone for 2027). The RX and NX each offer three hybrid trims including plug-ins, while the new ES350h is now the sole hybrid sedan.

Lincoln moved away from hybrids only to come running back—and they took a long way home. The brand’s two hybrid SUVs, the compact Corsair and mid-size two-row Nautilus, are plucked straight from China, since Ford hasn’t yet carved out factory space for these models in North America. They enjoy a substantial exterior refresh for 2027, too. Each comes with turbo inline-fours and all-wheel drive, while the Nautilus goes screen crazy with a 48-inch display hugging the bottom of the windshield.

While the CX-50 Hybrid uses a Toyota-based powertrain, the CX-90 Hybrid is all Mazda. It’s a nicely styled three-row plug-in hybrid SUV with an estimated 25 miles of electric range. The two-row CX-70 Hybrid is discontinued, but there’s a CX-5 Hybrid on the horizon, though it may not arrive until 2028.

Want a Le Mans racer as a comfortable supercar? There’s no better choice than a McLaren Artura, which has a howling twin-turbo V-6 that has the party trick of leaving and arriving in complete silence. With 11 miles of estimated electric range, it can go nearly three times as far on a charge than a Lamborghini Temerario can. The combined 690 horsepower and McLaren’s light-as-a-feather chassis are heavenly. Choose the coupe or a spider.

While AMG customers weren’t so enthusiastic about the C63 and its F1-derived four-cylinder plug-in hybrid powertrain, they’re happy plugging into turbo-sixes and turbo V-8s on the higher-end models. Every hybrid AMG is PHEV, whether it’s a sedan, wagon, SUV, convertible, or coupe. The E Performance trims of the SL and GT Coupe make more than 1000 pound-feet of torque.

Mercedes-Benz’s three hybrid models are all plug-in hybrids just like their AMG cousins, only less potent. The S580e is our personal favorite, as we were able to reach 58 miles of all-electric range on the highway, handily beating the factory estimate. The GLE500e also shares the same inline-six and delivers similar range, while the GLC350e has an inline-four. Like the AMGs, the GLE and S-class hybrids support DC fast charging, a rare feature on a PHEV.

Mitsubishi was first to market with a plug-in SUV, and it hasn’t really received due credit. Part of it is the premium price the Outlander PHEV commands and its so-so performance, though it’s updated for 2027 with more power. It also has plenty of features, decent interior quality, and a healthy 45-mile electric range. Along with the regular Outlander, it’s also the only three-row SUV in the compact segment.

As the only series hybrid in the mainstream segment, Nissan has made a big splash with the Rogue Hybrid after more than a decade without any gas-electric powertrain in its lineup. Think of the company’s e-Power hybrid setup like an extended-range EV where the gas engine serves only as a generator for the electric motors, but without the plug or the big battery. We like how it drives—a lot.

Porsche’s conventional hybrid powertrain sits in its most prized product, the 911, where the T-Hybrid installs one or two electric turbos and a small battery on the GTS and Turbo S. The models with the E-Hybrid badge are plug-in hybrids. The Panamera has three PHEV choices, including the Turbo’s V-8 powertrain shared with Bentley for up to 771 horsepower. The Cayenne Hybrid has either a V-6 hybrid setup or a similar V-8 setup in either the SUV or Coupe body style.

Panamera Turbo E-Hybrid / S Turbo E-Hybrid

#4289. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

#4288. Toyota is about to unveil its first extended-range EV, and it looks like the Highlander

Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.

Update 11/27/2026: Toyota announces the Highlander 9X as its first EREV (read more here).

The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).

Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.

EREVs use a smaller battery than a pure electric vehicle, while the engine is typically smaller than a PHEV. While they are quieter and often cheaper than a plug-in, EREVs are also less efficient than a pure EV.

A Nikkei report in September claimed that Toyota was preparing to begin production of its first EREV in China in Spring 2027.

It appears the rumors are true. Toyota’s joint venture in China, GAC Toyota, posted a preview on its Weibo account with the caption #Toyota doesn’t rush but range-extended.

Toyota didn’t confirm the name, but all signs point to it being the Highlander EREV. The blurry preview looks like the Highlander, and when translated into English, a part of the text below it reads “Cash in on the classics. Global flagship SUV. Not a quick fix, but a range extender.”

GAC Toyota will reveal the new EREV at the Guangzhou Motor Show on November 27. Check back for the full details.

According to the Nikkei report, Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in 2027. In 2028, it expects production to double to around 400,000 units.

While Toyota likely won’t bring the extended-range EV to the US, it is set to launch the fully electric version of its three-row Highlander in early 2027 (shown above on the left).

The all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.

Inside, the electric Toyota Highlander EV offers three rows of seating with room for up to seven passengers.

The three-row electric SUV will be built at Toyota’s manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky.

Like most foreign brands, Toyota is struggling to keep up with domestic brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery in China’s brutal auto market.

However, it’s Toyota’s gas and hybrid cars that are getting crushed by the competition. In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, about 19% fewer than in the same period last year.

After sales plunged nearly 20%, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower year-over-year sales, Toyota said the market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected.”

Meanwhile, BYD introduces a self-driving SUV with 600 miles of range that recharges in 10 minutes. These guys are toast.

Toyota looks to avoid the intensifying price war with pure electric vehicles in China. An EREV can potentially be offered at a premium, especially as a flagship SUV.

A company executive said (via Nikkei) that “Competition in China is intensifying as the market fixates on battery EVs, leading to price wars among automakers,” adding, “We need to take steps to avoid being dragged into that competition.”

Will an EREV help power Toyota’s comeback in China? Or is it late to the party once again? Share your thoughts in the comments.

#4287. Narrowed Focus: 1997 Toyota Camry LE Tested

One of America’s favorite family haulers gets a full makeover.

Over 3,000,000 sold! Call it the McCamry. Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go new-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995). Since its introduction here in 1983, Toyota has diligently smoothed up, slicked up, and suaved up the Camry till the only remaining awkwardness is the unlikely spelling of its name.

That won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite. We’re talking refinement of the Camry theme, not reinvention. In fact, the basic platform and powertrain carry on, though engineering improvements seem to touch every part of the car. It’s slightly bigger in each exterior dimension—0.7 inch longer, 0.4 inch wider, 2.1 inches longer in wheelbase; the same four­-cylinder and V-6 engines are modestly more powerful (up 8 hp in the four, up 6 hp in the V-6); and the interior has been upgraded to meet all the safety standards scheduled in the next few years, including the 1997 side-impact and 1999 head-­impact requirements. The aerodynamic drag coefficient has been improved to 0.30, from 0.33.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 01902

Toyota is, however, tightening the Camry’s focus. It’s available only as a four-door now in three trim levels: CE, LE, and XLE. Gone is the coupe, which won over just five percent of Camry buyers. Gone, too, is the station wagon, a shape that convinced only three per­cent of Camry buyers in its losing battle against the tide of minivans. (Production of a Camry-based minivan begins next spring.)

In the past, we’ve joked that the Camry’s personality is one of aggressive bland­ness. Unlike the frisky feeling of the Accord and the athletic tautness of the Dodge Intrepid, both of which come through loud and clear before you’ve driven to the first corner, the Camry’s subtlety grows on you over time. It’s smoother, softer, quieter than the others, less com­municative, less mechanical. Instead of talking to you in the very pleasant way of those others, it’s the silent type that, you soon notice, goes expertly about its job.

In this new Camry, Toyota sharpened the expertise without changing the per­sonality. It’s still a car that’s light to the touch: easy to steer, easy to brake. The ride is commendably free of harshness, thanks in part to mounting the suspension on isolated crossmembers front and rear. The four­-cylinder version, with its 195/70SR-14 tires, rides very smoothly and ignores almost completely the road textures that create so much droning in sporting cars. The V-6s come with 205/65HR-15s on six­-inch-wide wheels. These tires are noticeably harsher and noisier than those on the four-cylinder cars, though road nose is still quite reasonable when compared with other cars in this class. Road grip and handling predictability are well above the minimums we’d set for family cars.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 01902

The Camry V-6 has been one of the top performers in this class. The 1997 model gains six horsepower (now 194 hp at the same 5200 rpm as the previous peak), gets shorter final-drive gearing (3.93 versus 3.43), and weighs about the same as last year’s smaller car. Another performance plus: A manual transmission has returned to the V-6 lineup, available only on CE models. How­ever, our LE V-6 auto­matic was no quicker than the last LE V-6 we tested, managing 0 to 60 mph in 8.3 seconds. Expect the five-speed to trim that by about four-tenths.

On the road, the automatic’s eagerness to change down a gear or two when you press the pedal, even slightly, and the seamless smoothness of those changes give this car quick reflexes in traffic. The engine revs with the hushed moan of a Lexus. This year, traction control is optional on LE and XLE V-6 models. When it comes to powertrain pleasures, the Camry is world-class.

Still, it’s the more subtle details of pas­senger accommodation that make this Toyota a family favorite. In the previous­-generation Camry, our comparison tests show two adults fit in the back seat more comfortably than in some other brands up to 10 inches longer. We expect this Camry advantage to widen fractionally in this new model because both legroom and head­room in back are increased by a half-inch. Although the Camry is wider on the out­side, energy-absorbing padding to protect in side impacts takes up the extra space and, in certain spots, a little more. The Camry still has pockets in the front doors, unlike the Taurus, which sacrificed them for crash-protection equipment.

Those who wish to maximize rear-seat space should think twice about opting for power front seats (standard equipment on the top-of-the-line XLE). The manual­adjust buckets have excellent toeroom under them, which the power adjuster interrupts with a transverse bar. Tall folks won’t like that.

As in most modern sedans, the Camry has fold-forward rear seatbacks split one­-third and two-thirds, allowing the cargo compartment to be extended into the pas­senger area. Here’s another think-twice: Camrys equipped with the optional child seat—it’s built into the two-thirds section of the rear seat—have that section fixed in place, ruling out all but a narrow passage into the trunk.

At the rear, the trunklid opens wider and lower than before. Space inside, however, is a bit less in the new body—14.1 cubic feet versus 14.8 before. And the new car still has the conventional trunk hinges with the sickle arms that swing down into your luggage when the lid is closed.

Conventional is the right description for the new instrument panel, certainly more conventional than the old one, which tried to visually compartmentalize the cockpit by emphasizing a huge black field in front of the driver. That was the good part. The bad part was the deemphasized and totally boring padding it left for the passenger’s amusement. Now the all-new panel stretches its padding across the inte­rior in an equal-opportunity gesture that makes the interior seem brighter and wider. The glove box is 29 percent larger. The audio controls were raised to a mid­dash height, making them easy to see and reach. The climate controls have changed over to the increasingly common turn-to-adjust knobs. They’re large enough, and so obvious in their workings, that they are easy to operate in their less prominent location. The Camry continues to position its ignition switch in the dash where you can readily see it, instead of hiding it on the side of the steering column.

Toyota has proven itself to be the master of those little conveniences that add up to an exceptionally pleasing car. In this new Camry we see more clever trade-offs as the engineers cut costs, reduce weight, and usually end up serving the customer better, too. For example, the new front bumper cuts the part count nearly in half and saves weight, yet it increases protec­tion to 5 mph from 2.5. Inside, the seats recline in stepless increments now, and the buckets’ height adjusters use a single knob instead of two. Both of these changes cut costs, Toyota says. We say they make the car better, too. Models that previously would have had retracting antennas now have the antenna screened on the rear glass, saving weight and cost. The new Bosch anti-lock brake system weighs half as much as the old one.

Still, not every cost saver is a benefit. The LCD odometer is simply gray num­bers on a gray field, making it less visible than the glowing digits in competitors like the Chrysler Cirrus and the Dodge Stratus. And the new one-piece front-bumper cover now incorporates the grille into its overtly ordinary Rubbermaid-looking façade.

There’s been much speculation in the automotive-trade press about a possible price cut. Don’t hold your breath. Sales of the old Camry hit records earlier this year with no apparent price cutting. Were there sweeteners for the dealer? Sure, but other brands had them, too. Toyota knows all the tricks for selling cars without collapsing its price structure-tricks, we think, that mostly won’t be needed to move this shrewdly updated Camry.

#4286. Tesla quietly sets up a company at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

Tesla has registered a new German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.

Neither company confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.

The company is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.

It didn’t start out as a Tesla company. The register shows it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.

Business Insider Germany, which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, says three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.

The HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.

Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.

Local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.

Today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either company.

EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG said it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.

But EMAG has also been chasing a new market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts: flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.

The first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG says its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.

That’s right where Tesla says it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time. Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it showed in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot. At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.

Tesla moving directly into precision tooling highlights a brutal reality for robotics founders: software gets the spotlight, but high-tolerance actuator supply chains dictate your unit economics and scale. Building physical AI means mastering industrial manufacturing long before mass production begins. When navigating high-stakes hardware trade-offs and specialized talent, having early backers who have built hardware companies matters. Grove Ventures works hands-on from pre-seed with deeptech and AI founders, offering real operator experience to help scale complex physical architectures.

Tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025, along with about 300 of its employees.

Tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin.

Tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

#4285. Infinity Nikki 2.0 launches with a whole new region, archery skills, and a new theme song by original Wicked actor Idina Menzel

Infinity Nikki's version 2.0 is the game's biggest evolution yet, transforming almost every part of it.

Infinity Nikki has officially evolved into a bigger, more feature-rich game. After months of waiting, version 2.0 has arrived to bring massive overhauls - and plenty of new content - to the dress-up RPG.

The update, available now on all platforms, is dubbed Terra’s Call. It adds a new region, Itzaland, to the game’s world. It also reshapes the rest of Miraland.

Itzaland is only the tip of the iceberg. Elderwood Forest and Spira are the region's two new areas, with more to be unlocked down the line. This patch also upgrades several core mechanics, including combat and exploration. There’s a suite of new traversal abilities, too, like grappling, low-gravity and even gigantification.

Archery is a new addition to combat, and you’ll spot new combat companions as part of the adaptive energy mechanics. Terra’s Call clearly has a focus on interactivity with the game’s world, to make it feel more alive and lived-in.

There’s a host of new interactions you can have with cute creatures like singing mushrooms, and wall-climbing snails. Version 2.0 also makes for a great starting point for new players as both main and side stories are now available for free.

It wouldn’t be a dress-up game without a host of new fashion sets, and outfits, of course - and there's plenty here, both free and paid. The launch of the new update also kicks off several in-game events, including some that celebrate the game’s second anniversary, and Nikki’s birthday.

Infold also recently announced that Idina Menzel — the actor who originated the roles of Elphaba in Wicked and Elsa in Frozen — will be singing the brand-new theme song for Version 2.0. You can listen to that on the official Infinity Nikki YouTube channel, where you can also watch a behind-the-scenes interview with Ms Menzel.

#4283. Mice slept 70% less after scientists switched off these brain cells

Why does being awake for too long make us increasingly desperate for sleep? Scientists at the University of Basel in Switzerland have identified two groups of brain cells in mice that become more active the longer the animals remain awake. These neurons play a critical role in creating the pressure to sleep, offering new clues about how the brain regulates our need for rest.

The longer we go without sleep, the more difficult it becomes to stay awake. This buildup of sleep pressure, often called sleep drive, helps ensure that extended periods of wakefulness are followed by longer and deeper sleep. Although sleep is essential for survival, exactly how the brain measures time spent awake and converts that information into an increasing need for sleep has remained a mystery.

Researchers led by Professor Alex Schier at the Biozentrum, University of Basel, have now identified brain cells that help regulate this process. The work was conducted in collaboration with scientists from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Auburn University.

"We have identified neuronal populations that monitor prolonged wakefulness and actively promote sleep," says Alex Schier. "This is an important missing piece of the puzzle in understanding why we become sleepy."

Scientists Identify Brain Cells That Drive Sleep Pressure

To investigate how sleep pressure develops, the team studied patterns of brain activity in mice under three different conditions: normal cycles of sleeping and waking, extended sleep deprivation, and recovery sleep. By comparing these patterns, they identified brain regions whose activity changed according to how long the animals had been awake.

Within one of these regions, the brainstem, researchers pinpointed two groups of neurons involved in controlling sleep drive. Known as GABAergic and serotonergic neurons, both groups became progressively more active as the mice remained awake. Their activity then decreased once the animals fell asleep.

The next question was whether these neurons simply tracked how long the mice had been awake or actually helped create the growing need for sleep.

Experiments revealed that the neurons were directly involved in driving sleep. When researchers artificially activated both groups, the mice slept longer and more deeply, showing the same type of recovery sleep normally seen after extended wakefulness. When the neurons were inhibited, however, the animals slept substantially less and were able to remain awake and alert.

"These neurons do not simply signal that an animal has been awake," says Schier. "Our experiments show that they are crucial to promote sleep, and that they may be key components of the neural circuitry that generates sleep drive."

The results provide particularly strong evidence that certain neurons activated during wakefulness do more than register lost sleep. They actively help generate the pressure that eventually pushes the brain toward sleep.

Mice Sleep 70% Less When Key Neurons Are Inhibited

Further experiments produced an especially surprising result. When scientists suppressed both groups of neurons for an extended period, the mice slept approximately 70% less than normal.

Even more unexpectedly, most of these animals did not display some of the serious behavioral problems typically associated with prolonged sleep deprivation. Despite getting dramatically less sleep, many avoided impairments that researchers would ordinarily expect.

These findings suggest that the identified neurons influence not only the amount of time animals spend sleeping, but also how strongly the pressure to sleep increases during wakefulness.

Rather than simply responding to exhaustion, the brain appears to use specific neural circuits to actively regulate the growing need for rest.

Understanding these circuits could open important new avenues for studying sleep and its effects on the body. Researchers now hope to determine how the identified neurons communicate with other brain regions and what molecular processes allow them to generate sleep pressure.

"Future studies could reveal how these neurons interact with the rest of the brain, and how sleep drive is generated at the molecular level," says Dr. William Joo, first author of the study. "Our ability to stably transform sleep behavior also allows us to explore adaptations to long-term sleep loss - this may eventually reveal ways to confer resilience to sleep deprivation and other physiological challenges."

The findings establish that GABAergic and serotonergic neurons in the brainstem become increasingly active during prolonged wakefulness and play an essential role in promoting sleep.

Determining exactly how the brain makes sleep increasingly difficult to resist remains a major objective of sleep research. Beyond improving scientists' understanding of sleep disorders, this discovery could help explain how the nervous system adapts to extended wakefulness and other physical challenges.

Ultimately, a clearer understanding of the brain circuits responsible for sleep pressure could inspire new treatments and potentially reveal ways to improve resilience to sleep deprivation.

Materials provided by University of Basel. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
